setter.name: Trevor
setter.evidence: The lead was sourced and qualified by Trevor himself over Instagram DMs, not by a setter. The prospect: 'I saw some videos from Trevor, some workouts that I tried... And then Trevor got in contact with me. So and then he started [chatting] and I felt like it was good' (00:12:35), and later 'because I got contacted by Trevor and he got speaking with me and I was curious to see how it works... because he contacted me, I took the opportunity to have the meeting' (00:40:09). The rep cited those notes twice: 'I already got some information from Trevor' and 'I heard from Trevor that you also do some running, right?'

prospect.name: José
prospect.location: Milan, Italy; originally from Ecuador and recently relocated
prospect.occupation: Telemetry and data analyst for a go-kart racing team. Formerly a go-kart driver himself, stopped racing on moving to Italy. Freelance or invoice-based, travelling with the team roughly half the time; physically active work including erecting a large tent and moving heavy equipment.
prospect.family_status: Married; refers to ordering food with his wife and cooking at home together
prospect.training_background: Active his whole life through go-kart racing but never trained seriously with weights. Started working out in December, inconsistently at first, then more consistently around two to three months ago using a free outdoor calisthenics gym in the park by his home. Plateaued because he cannot reduce his own bodyweight to make the movements achievable — can manage about two unassisted pull-ups. Bought an adjustable kettlebell one and a half weeks before the call after finding a 16 kg bell far too heavy in the shop, and is currently training at 12 kg, four or five sessions so far. Also runs a two-mile circuit before strength work. Describes himself, and is described by the rep, as already lean.
prospect.medical: Right shoulder aches intermittently following a fall down stairs roughly a year earlier — 'sometimes I get a weird ache, but it's not like something really serious'. Reports severe and prolonged hamstring soreness after his first goblet squats: 'the part behind my leg, between my knee and my waist... it hurt a lot, and it hurt for a whole week', and asked directly whether that was normal and whether he could push through it. The rep said a week is too much and attributed it to form or weight, but no assessment or resolution followed. Previously had knee pain from poor running form, which he says he corrected himself. Smoked cannabis for around ten years and quit three to four months before the call, using training as the replacement behaviour. No health conditions were asked about.

signals: Already lean and active, seeking capability rather than rescue — the rep's own summary, unchallenged: 'you're already lean, right?' / 'Yes'
Frames physique as a by-product rather than the goal: 'once I start and feel stronger, then my physique will also change, but I think that's secondary'
Self-directed and already executing — bought equipment, built a routine, corrected his own running form, and quit a ten-year habit unaided

Counter-signals keeping confidence moderate: on the price criterion he is the opposite of an optimizer — 'it's not like I have a lot of extra money. So I'm mostly getting by' — and at 27 with no real lifting history he is closer to a first-time builder than to someone recovering a former peak

goals.text: Get meaningfully stronger — named as the primary goal, ahead of appearance
Learn correct form so he is working the right muscles and can progress the weight with confidence
Avoid injury, which he raises unprompted as his main fear
Make the physical parts of his job easier — 'when putting up the tent, there's some heavy stuff we have to move around... it shouldn't feel so hard'
Feel healthier after a sedentary first year in Italy
Become more athletic and defined as a by-product of getting stronger
Keep training as the replacement for a ten-year cannabis habit he quit three to four months ago
Build enough strength that progression becomes possible at all — cannot yet reach the starting point for bodyweight work

pains.text: Plateaued on calisthenics because bodyweight cannot be reduced — 'I can't lower the weight. So I feel like I still don't have the strength to work with my body. So if I'm not at the starting point, it's like I can't progress'
Does not know whether his kettlebell technique is correct and is afraid of injuring himself — 'mostly I'm afraid of getting injured'
Hamstring pain lasting a full week after his first goblet squats, with no idea whether it is normal or whether to push through
Variable freelance income with two months of no work ahead and a first-year tax bill higher than budgeted
Nutrition falls out of his control on team travel — 'when I'm with the team, it's a bit harder because mostly for dinner, we always go to restaurants'
Right shoulder aches intermittently after a fall down stairs a year ago

Compares himself unfavourably with more experienced people at the outdoor gym

objections.raw_quote: Yeah. I mean, it's a bit out of my budget, I think.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it immediately — 'just a triple check, right? Outside of the investment part, do you feel like, yeah, I do want to get started with this?' — then reframed to a how-question and ran a genuine financial picture: cash available (one to two thousand), month-end surplus (variable, none for two months), and credit and third-party financing, which he ruled out himself once he learned the prospect is Ecuadorian rather than American.

objections.raw_quote: Well, still, even with the finance, like, it wouldn't be a responsible decision. For me, in my current position... because right now, since I moved to a new country and everything has been going quite okay, but it's not like I have a lot of extra money. So I'm mostly getting by.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and disqualified explicitly: 'honestly speaking, I wouldn't advise you to go start with this at the moment, because I don't want to put you in a financial position.' Then routed to the lower tier at $200 a month or $2,000 a year, recommending the monthly option specifically because it is cancellable.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, well, I have to think about it here. So I wouldn't say yes right now.
objections.rep_response: Probed four times without pressuring — asked what he specifically meant, whether it was worth waiting six months physically, what had made him take the meeting at all, and whether the risk was real. Got a concrete and credible answer each time, then accepted and offered to send the link anyway.

objections.raw_quote: it's really risky like I said this is my first year paying the taxes, it's really difficult the taxes here so it was from the beginning a lot higher than I was thinking so I have to pay a lot more than I had budgeted for initially plus my job is really variable and we have the next two months without doing any work.
objections.rep_response: 'Yeah, that's understandable. I don't want to put you in a position.' Sent the Primal University link and a training video and left the door open for August or sooner.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No instalment structure was offered on the $6,000 tier. Third-party financing was raised and immediately ruled out: 'if you had a credit card and yet you still had your credit score, we could have potentially done it on a third party, but that wouldn't be the case if you're not from America.'

evidence: No payment on either tier. The $6,000 programme was withdrawn by the rep on affordability grounds, and the $200/month tier was declined for now: 'I have to think about it here. So I wouldn't say yes right now.'
Rep to send the Primal University link and a training video by WhatsApp; the prospect asked for it — 'Yeah, you can send it over and I can check it'.
Prospect named end of August as his decision point, contingent on two months of no work and an unquantified first tax bill.

Counter-evidence toward a future close: engagement was high throughout, all three pillars were accepted, and he confirmed belief without hedging — 'definitely. I think everything combined will be really good.'

Counter-evidence against: intent was low from the start by his own account — 'because he contacted me, I took the opportunity to have the meeting' — this was an outbound lead, and even $200 a month was outside what he would commit to.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send a Primal University link and a kettlebell video on WhatsApp; prospect to reassess at the end of August once his tax liability is clear and work resumes, with an open invitation to start sooner.

notable.note: The cleanest conduct in the batch on the commercial side and one of the sharper clinical gaps. The rep ran a full financial picture, concluded the prospect could not responsibly afford the programme, said so out loud — 'honestly speaking, I wouldn't advise you to go start with this at the moment' — and routed him to the $200/month tier, naming it as Primal University. That is the same tier withheld from two prospects in this batch who also could not fund $6,000, which makes its application across the week inconsistent rather than absent. Clinically, the prospect reported a week of hamstring pain after his first goblet squats at 12 kg, asked twice whether it was normal and whether to push through, and got a heuristic rather than an answer; he was then sent an unsupervised training video and told the self-directed product 'is going to help you with absolutely not getting injured'. The rep also read the prospect's full mobile number back over the recording, the second time in this batch.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion of short turns and several inverted passages. Clear examples: at 00:04:11 to 00:04:29 the rep's explanation of why he asks about hips and backs sits under José's label while José's confirmation sits under the rep's; at 00:04:38 the rep's label carries José's description of his own breakfast; at 00:08:03 José's label carries the rep's recital of his height and weight; at 00:10:28 the rep's question about his role in the team is inside José's block. The stretch from roughly 00:25:10 to 00:28:31 is a single unpunctuated block containing the whole training and nutrition presentation plus José's replies, and 00:38:55 to 00:42:09 is similar. Roles read from content throughout. One transcription oddity: 'Richard' appears at 00:28:00 where the rep is addressing José, and 'Jack' recurs where 'check' is meant.
